title: Security exception
description: A documented, time-bounded decision not to fix a security finding immediately. SOIF Part 1 §45. This schema is HAND-WRITTEN and lives beside the files it governs rather than under `schemas/`, because `schemas/` is generated from the package's models by `python -m synapse_cdm.schemas` and a hand-written file there would be deleted by the next regeneration. An exception is not package surface: no code imports it, and the two consumers that read it (`gates/codeql_gate.py` and the pip-audit step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) read the directory, not the package.

identifier.description: The finding's own id, exactly as the tool that reports it prints it: a CodeQL rule id (`py/sql-injection`), a GitHub advisory (`GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`), a PyPA advisory (`PYSEC-2026-1`) or a CVE. This is the string the consumers match on, so it is the tool's spelling and never a paraphrase.

affected_package.description: The distribution the finding is in, or `synapse-cdm` itself when the finding is in this repository's own code.

version_range.description: The versions this exception covers, as a PEP 440 specifier (`>=2.0,<2.2`) or the literal `*` when the finding is in this repository's own code and versions do not apply. An exception with no range is an exception with no end, which is what §45 forbids.

risk.description: What an attacker gets if this is exploited HERE, in this repository's use of the package — not the advisory's generic wording. Thirty characters is a floor against a one-word entry, not a target.

reason.description: Why it is not being fixed now, and what has to change for it to be fixed. “No fix available upstream” is a reason; “low priority” is not.

owner.description: A person or team that answers for this exception. A GitHub handle or an email address; never `unassigned`, never a role nobody holds.

expiry.description: The date after which this exception is no longer valid, ISO 8601. `tests/test_cdm_security_exceptions.py` fails the suite the day this passes — unconditionally and with no flag — which is what makes §45's “no permanent undocumented exemptions” enforced rather than intended.

created.description: The date this exception was written, ISO 8601. Kept so that the interval between `created` and `expiry` is readable rather than inferred.

references.description: At least one URL: the advisory, the upstream issue, the CodeQL query's documentation. An exception with no reference is a decision with no evidence behind it.
